I'm just starting into it and have read the author's thesis statement.

I generally like his passion, enthusiasm, and way with metaphor but I kinda think he's begging the question by assuming things like consciousness, math, music, and art are actually meaningful instead of merely complex and layered or self referential (looping). Basically, he rubs the Nihilist in me.

I'm also interested in figuring out his interest in looping/recursion themselves as as vehicles to "meaning" as opposed to any complex network. I suspect a web would be just as meaningful in his sense and I'm looking forward to reading why (if?) he disagrees.

tl;dr: Gödel, Escher, Bach looks pretty cool but why loops? Thoughts on the book?

The book is meant to be an "experience," and it was an enjoyable one for me. Most people don't know as much as he does about all four of the subjects discussed (philosophy, art, math, and music), and certainly, few can draw the connections Hofstadter did as elegantly and with such good humor.

However, in Hofstadter's own opinion, GEB failed. It was received as a kind of hodgepodge of information, whereas he wanted it to be a deep and personal reflection on the nature of "the self." To fix this "error," he wrote I am a Strange Loop in 2007. If you do read GEB, you should probably read Strange Loop to get a truly complete experience. Or, you might want to skip GEB altogether and go for the "correct" book.

If you do decide to finish GEB, my tip would be not to take it too seriously. Enjoy it and skip around -- you don't have to read every single word to get a great experience. :)

Edit: his focus on recursion has a lot to do with his theory of how an AI should be constructed, which you get later in the book. His model of learning and thought is heavily based on this concept. Unfortunately, my understanding is that more contemporary AI theory doesn't really resemble his approach. Nevertheless, it's a great tour de force in metacognition.

I'm enjoying it and I feel it's pretty easy to understand so far. I don't quite get why people find it so puzzling. He says it's a metaphorical fugue and proceeds to present the same theme (or at least variations on it) in different voices.

I do think he's making a bit of a leap though when he thinks recursive and self referential systems have a self on the same sense as consciousness. I'll see if I still think that at the end though.

Non-symbolic approaches are more like amalgams of very basic, "dumb" functions, such as facial recognition software, that come together to resemble, or "behave like," an intelligence.
